Call an operation of the Voidhash API as yourself and print its JSON response.

An operation of a project is called on the project commands act on here ('voidhash status' shows
which), on --project, or on the one --path projectId=<id> names. An answer of 400 or above ends the
command with the exit code of its status: 2 for 400, 3 for 401, 4 for 404, else 1.

Usage:
  voidhash api call <operation> [flags]

Arguments:
  operation  The operation's id from 'voidhash api list', such as webhooks.list

Flags:
      --body <json>         The request body as json, inline or as @file.json
      --environment <production|test|all>
                            Purchases the call sees: production (the default; production purchases,
                            and store sandbox ones when they unlock production), test (store sandbox
                            and test purchases, as a test key reads) or all
  -h, --help                Show help for this command
      --path <name=value>   A path parameter as name=value (can be repeated)
      --project <project>   Project to act on: its id, slug, organization/slug or name (default:
                            this directory's project, then your default project)
      --query <name=value>  A query parameter as name=value; a repeated name is a list (can be
                            repeated)

Global flags:
  -d, --debug              Print each request and full error detail to standard error
      --no-color           Print without colors (also when NO_COLOR is set)
      --profile <profile>  Use a named config profile: its settings override the base config
                           (default: VOIDHASH_PROFILE)

Examples:
  voidhash api call webhooks.list --query limit=5
  voidhash api call webhooks.get --path webhookId=wh_123
  voidhash api call webhooks.create --body '{"name": "Orders", "url": "https://example.com/hook"}'
  voidhash api call products.create --body @product.json --project acme/app
